title: Document the latency and fairness trade-off of bounded history state admission
outcome: The history capture contract explains the bounded state-lock admission policy, including up to25ms sampling latency on brief contention, its interaction with the original operation budget and the established poison-recovery behavior. Any later optimization preserves the operation budget and transcript coherence.
acceptance: The history capture contract explicitly explains why state admission uses bounded retries for resident and persisted pages and describes the latency/fairness trade-off.
Any implementation adjustment retains the original whole-operation deadline and coherent transcript authority; no unbounded first-lock wait is introduced.
